purpose: Calibrate memory-related mechanisms missing from the template system. Sleep-dependent consolidation and context-dependent recall are critical for educational, healthcare, and workplace design but lack architectural parameterization.

target_templates.name: Sleep Consolidation & Restoration
target_templates.mechanism: Sleep-dependent memory consolidation as affected by bedroom/sleeping environment. Slow-wave sleep → hippocampal replay → neocortical consolidation.
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Bedrooms, healthcare recovery rooms, dormitories, hotels. Environmental features that optimize sleep architecture directly affect learning and recovery.

target_templates.name: Context-Dependent Memory
target_templates.mechanism: Environmental context reinstated at retrieval → 20-40% recall advantage. Encoding specificity principle applied to architecture.
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Educational facilities, training centers, workplaces. Designing learning spaces to optimize later recall through context reinstatement.

constructs_to_calibrate.name: sleep_architecture_sensitivity
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Relationship between room features and sleep stage proportions
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: many studies on temperature, light, noise, but not integrated

constructs_to_calibrate.name: consolidation_window
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Critical period after learning when sleep affects retention
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: well-established in sleep science, not applied to architecture

constructs_to_calibrate.name: context_reinstatement_benefit
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Recall improvement when learning and test contexts match

constructs_to_calibrate.name: context_distinctiveness
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Degree to which environment features create distinctive context

constructs_to_calibrate.name: encoding_depth_environment
constructs_to_calibrate.description: How environmental features affect depth of encoding

key_papers.contribution: Classic underwater/land encoding study. Established context-dependent memory effect size.
Meta-analysis of environmental context-dependent memory. Effect size d=0.28.
Review of sleep-dependent memory consolidation mechanisms.
Effects of thermal environment on sleep quality and architecture.

design_features: Consistency between learning and testing spaces
population_sensitivity: Children benefit more from context reinstatement
Elderly show reduced sleep consolidation efficiency
Students under stress show impaired consolidation

calibration_protocol: 1. Define architectural features that create distinctive contexts
2. Map room features to sleep architecture metrics
3. Parameterize context reinstatement benefit by context similarity
5. Define WIS conversion from memory parameters
output_deliverables: Updated T10, T23 template JSON files with calibrated parameters
Interaction coefficients with L templates (light), MAT templates (thermal)
